exam.name: SCOR
exam.title: Implementing and Operating Cisco Security Core Technologies v2.0

objectives.text: Explain attack threats against on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments such as viruses, trojans, DoS/DDoS, phishing, rootkits, man-in-the middle, malware, data breaches, insecure APIs, compromised credentials, PQC, and AI

Describe security vulnerabilities and exploits such as software bugs, weak and/or hardcoded passwords, OWASP top ten, missing encryption ciphers, buffer overflow, path traversal, cross-site scripting/forgery, SQL injection, and identification and prioritization using CVEs and CVSS scores
Describe vulnerabilities in AI/LLM models such as prompt injection, system prompt leakage, vector and embedding weaknesses, and supply chain
Describe the controls used to protect against phishing and social engineering attacks

Describe cryptography security components such as hashing, encryption, PKI, SSL, TLS, QUIC, MASQUE, IPsec, NAT-T IPv4 for IPsec, preshared key, certificate-based authorization, and post-quantum cryptography
Describe site-to-site and remote access VPN deployment types such as virtual tunnel interfaces, standards-based IPsec, SSL VPN, DMVPN, FlexVPN, and GETVPN
Describe security intelligence authoring, sharing, and consumption
Describe zero trust architecture
Describe defense in depth strategy such as Secure Architecture for Everyone (SAFE)
Interpret scripts used to call security appliances APIs in a language such as Python
Describe network security solutions and deployment models that provide intrusion prevention and firewall capabilities
Describe security monitoring and telemetry technologies

Configure network infrastructure security methods (network segmentation using VLANs or SGTs; Layer 2 and port security; DHCP snooping; Dynamic ARP inspection; storm control; and defenses against MAC, ARP, VLAN hopping, STP, and DHCP rogue attacks)
Select management options for network security solutions (single vs. multidevice manager, in-band vs. out-of-band, on-premises vs. cloud with Cisco Security Cloud Control)
Describe CIS benchmarks for hardening devices such as Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD) and Cisco IOS XE
Troubleshoot AAA for device and network access such as TACACS+ and RADIUS
Configure secure network management of perimeter security and infrastructure devices such as SNMPv3, NetConf, RestConf, APIs, secure syslog, and NTP with authentication
Implement access control policies, AVC, URL filtering, malware protection, and intrusion prevention using Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD)
Configure site-to-site and remote access VPN using Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD) and Cisco Secure Client
Troubleshoot VPN tunnel establishment on Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD)
Describe security responsibility within common Cloud Shared Responsibility Models
Select security capabilities, deployment models, cloud security frameworks, and policy management to secure the cloud
Select security solutions for cloud environments (public; private; hybrid; community cloud; NIST 800-145 SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS; and Cloud Access Security Broker)
Describe network, application, and data security in cloud environments with solutions such as Cisco Multicloud Defense and Cisco Secure Workload
Configure Splunk to ingest cloud logging and monitoring data from other security solutions
Describe application and workload security concepts including eBPF
Describe DevSecOps (Infrastructure as Code security, CI/CD pipeline, container orchestration, and secure software development)
Describe Security Service Edge (SSE) and Secure Access Service Edge (SASE)
Configure Cisco Secure Access Secure Internet Access
Configure Cisco Secure Access Secure Private Access
Configure data loss prevention and AI guardrails for secure internet access
Interpret Cisco Secure Access Investigate scores and indicators
Describe Endpoint Protection Platforms (EPP) and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions
Describe endpoint device management and asset inventory systems such as MDM
Describe endpoint posture assessment solutions to ensure endpoint security
Describe endpoint protection and detection security with solutions such as Cisco Secure Client and Cisco Secure Malware Analytics
Configure endpoint antimalware protection using Cisco Secure Endpoint
Interpret Cisco Secure Endpoint malware detection events
Configure email security features with Cisco Security Email Threat Defense
Describe identity management and secure network access concepts such as guest services, profiling, posture assessment, and BYOD
Describe device compliance and application control
Configure network access control mechanisms such as 802.1X and MAB with Cisco Identity Services Engine
Configure network access with CoA
Explain exfiltration techniques such as DNS tunneling, HTTPS, email, FTP/SSH/SCP/SFTP, ICMP, Messenger, IRC, NTP, and cloud storage
Describe network visibility and enforcement using telemetry and native AI/ML capabilities with XDR and SIEM/SOAR platforms such as Splunk and Cisco XDR
Describe Cisco Duo in a zero-trust security architecture (Trust Monitor, MFA, Device Trust, health checks, Adaptive Access policies, SSO, and CII)
Describe managing, orchestrating, and automating security information and events with Splunk

lectures.title: Network Security: Firewalls, IPS, and Visibility
lectures.seo_title: SCOR 350-701 Network Security Notes: Firewall, IPS & Telemetry
lectures.description: Free CCNP Security notes for SCOR 350-701 v2.0 topics 2.1 and 2.2: firewall and IPS deployment models, FTD modes, NetFlow, SNMPv3 and telemetry.
lectures.dek: What enforces, where it goes, and how you see what got past it: firewall and IPS solutions and deployment models (2.1) and security monitoring and telemetry (2.2).

lectures.title: Segmentation & Layer 2 Hardening
lectures.seo_title: SCOR 2.3 Layer 2 Security: VLAN Hopping, DHCP Snooping, DAI
lectures.description: Free CCNP Security notes for SCOR 350-701 v2.0 topic 2.3: VLAN hopping, port security, BPDU Guard, DHCP snooping, DAI, storm control, PVLANs and SGTs.
lectures.dek: How to think about Layer 2 trust, then every switch defense in SCOR 2.3: VLANs and SGTs, trunk hardening, port security, STP guards, DHCP snooping, DAI and storm control.

lectures.title: Management Options, CIS Benchmarks & AAA
lectures.seo_title: SCOR 2.4-2.6: Security Cloud Control, CIS Benchmarks, TACACS+ vs RADIUS
lectures.description: Free CCNP Security notes for SCOR 350-701 v2.0 topics 2.4 to 2.6: FMC vs. Security Cloud Control, out-of-band management, CIS Benchmarks, TACACS+ and RADIUS.
lectures.dek: Who manages your security devices, how they stay hardened, and who may log in: single vs. multidevice managers, Security Cloud Control, CIS Benchmarks and drift, then AAA with TACACS+ and RADIUS, troubleshooting included.

lectures.title: Secure Network Management: SNMPv3, NETCONF, RESTCONF, NTP & Syslog
lectures.seo_title: SCOR 2.7: SNMPv3, NETCONF vs RESTCONF, NTP Authentication, Secure Syslog
lectures.description: Free CCNP Security notes for SCOR 350-701 v2.0 topic 2.7: SNMPv3 authPriv, NETCONF vs. RESTCONF and YANG, APIs, authenticated NTP and syslog over TLS.
lectures.dek: Every management protocol has an insecure past and a secure replacement: SNMPv3 authPriv, NETCONF and RESTCONF over SSH and HTTPS, authenticated NTP and syslog over TLS. How each works, how to configure it on IOS XE, and how to read its failures.

lectures.title: Attack Threats, Vulnerabilities & the CIA Triad
lectures.seo_title: SCOR 350-701 Threats & Vulnerabilities: OWASP, APIs, AI, PQC (1.1-1.3)
lectures.description: Free CCNP Security notes for SCOR 350-701 v2.0 topics 1.1 to 1.3: malware, DDoS, OWASP and API risks, CVSS, post-quantum crypto, LLM vulnerabilities.
lectures.dek: Take any attack apart into actor, vector, vulnerability, exploit, payload and impact. Malware, DDoS, on-path attacks, OWASP and API risks, CVE and CVSS, stolen credentials, the quantum threat and LLM vulnerabilities, all tied back to the CIA triad.

labs.title: Segmentation & Layer 2 Hardening Lab
labs.seo_title: Free Packet Tracer Lab: Layer 2 Switch Hardening (CCNP SCOR 2.3)
labs.description: Free Packet Tracer lab for CCNP Security SCOR 2.3: harden a 2960 switch with dead VLANs, trunk lockdown, port security, BPDU Guard and protected ports.
labs.dek: Download a working but insecure switched network and harden it step by step: management baseline, VLANs, trunks, port security, BPDU Guard, protected ports and unused-port lockdown.

labs.title: Layer 2 Attack Prevention Lab
labs.cta: Attack, protect, prove: rogue DHCP, ARP spoofing, rogue switches and broadcast storms
labs.seo_title: Free Packet Tracer Lab: DHCP Snooping, DAI, BPDU Guard (CCNP SCOR 2.3)
labs.description: Free CCNP Security Packet Tracer lab: stop rogue DHCP, ARP spoofing and rogue switches with DHCP snooping, DAI, BPDU Guard, Root Guard and storm control.
labs.dek: Attack a small switched network, then defend it phase by phase with DHCP snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection, BPDU Guard, Root Guard and storm control. Real Packet Tracer output explained line by line, with every real IOS vs. Packet Tracer difference called out.

labs.title: AAA with TACACS+ Lab: Configure and Troubleshoot
labs.cta: Build TACACS+ login with a local fallback, then break it three ways and read each fault from debug tacacs
labs.seo_title: Free TACACS+ Lab: Configure and Troubleshoot AAA on Cisco IOS (SCOR 2.6)
labs.description: Free CCNP Security lab: configure TACACS+ with a local fallback on Cisco IOS, then troubleshoot a wrong key, wrong password and wrong server IP with debug tacacs.
labs.dek: Build TACACS+ authentication on a real IOS router one verified step at a time, prove a server-only user can log in, then break it three ways and read each fault straight from debug tacacs.

environments.name: Cisco Modeling Labs
environments.note: IOSv or IOL router plus an Ubuntu node running a TACACS+ daemon, or an ISE node. Recommended.

environments.name: DevNet / dCloud
environments.note: Hosted labs and demos with IOS XE and ISE already built.

environments.name: Your own gear
environments.note: Any IOS or IOS XE router and a Linux VM running a TACACS+ server.

environments.name: Packet Tracer
environments.note: Basic AAA only. No debug tacacs, so the troubleshooting half doesn't work.

labs.title: AAA and Device Hardening Lab (Packet Tracer)
labs.cta: Harden two sites, log in with TACACS+ and RADIUS against one server, then break AAA seven ways
labs.seo_title: Free Packet Tracer Lab: TACACS+, RADIUS and Device Hardening (CCNP SCOR 2.6)
labs.description: Free CCNP Security Packet Tracer lab: TACACS+ and RADIUS logins with local fallback, SSH, NTP, syslog, OSPF MD5 and switch hardening, plus 7 AAA faults.
labs.dek: Take a working two-site network with zero security to a CIS-style baseline, move admin logins onto one AAA server over TACACS+ and RADIUS, watch the packets in Simulation mode, then break it seven ways and explain each result.

labs.title: SNMPv3 Lab: authPriv, snmpwalk and snmpset
labs.cta: Build SNMPv3 authPriv on IOS XE, walk the router from Linux, then rename it with one snmpset
labs.seo_title: Free SNMPv3 Lab: authPriv Users, Views, snmpwalk and snmpset (SCOR 2.7)
labs.description: Free CCNP Security lab: configure SNMPv3 authPriv on IOS XE with ACLs, views, groups and users, then test it with snmpwalk and snmpset from Linux.
labs.dek: Configure SNMPv3 with SHA and AES on an IOS XE router, poll it from a Linux host with snmpwalk, change its hostname with snmpset, and read every SNMPv3 error.
labs.tool: IOS XE router + Linux with Net-SNMP

labs.title: NETCONF and RESTCONF Lab: YANG Data with curl and Python
labs.cta: Turn on RESTCONF and NETCONF, check the YANG processes, then read the router with curl, requests and ncclient
labs.seo_title: Free NETCONF and RESTCONF Lab on IOS XE with curl and Python (SCOR 2.7)
labs.description: Free CCNP Security lab: enable RESTCONF and NETCONF on IOS XE, verify the YANG processes, and read interfaces, OSPF and the full config with curl and Python.
labs.dek: Enable RESTCONF over HTTPS and NETCONF over SSH on IOS XE, confirm the YANG processes are ready, and read live data with curl, Python requests and ncclient.
labs.tool: IOS XE router + Linux with Python 3

labs.title: Authenticated NTP Lab: HMAC-SHA-256 Between Two Routers
labs.cta: Make one router an authenticated NTP server and watch the other go from stratum 16 to synchronized
labs.seo_title: Free NTP Authentication Lab: hmac-sha2-256 on Cisco IOS XE (SCOR 2.7)
labs.description: Free CCNP Security lab: configure authenticated NTP with hmac-sha2-256 between two IOS XE routers, verify the sync and the key match, and troubleshoot it.
labs.dek: Configure an authenticated NTP server and client on IOS XE, watch the client go from stratum 16 to synchronized, and prove the key match from the debug and association detail.

environments.name: DevNet / dCloud
environments.note: Any reservable topology with two IOS XE routers.

environments.note: Two IOS or IOS XE routers; older releases may offer md5 keys only.
